english.title: Fraudulently load a vehicle before customs clearance made
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), a vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY THE VEHICLE..), having been required to obtain clearance from the United Kingdom under section 64 of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979 and goods, namely **(..SPECIFY THE GOODS..), having been

(A)_[loaded]_
(B)_[made waterborne for loading]_

with fraudulent intent into that vehicle before application for clearance to depart the United Kingdom was made, you were concerned therein with knowledge of that intent
english.legislation: Contrary to section 64(7) and (8) of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979.

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding £20,000 or of three times the value of the goods whichever is the greater.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex

libra.complexpenaltydetails: On summary conviction the maximum financial penalty is £20,000 or of three times the value of the goods whichever is the greater
